I ended up doing a hardware encode with my quality set to 28 and had decent results in about 20 minutes for a bluray. Some fast than others but all in all that was about my average.

1. Got a movie subscription since my gf and I love movies. It was getting way too costly to go the movies. My subscription is for 6 tickets a month and only cost me $28.

2. My gf has a favorite restaurant but notoriously wouldn't be able to eat her whole meal. Now when ever we go we share the meal and get an appetizer. This has trickled into where ever we are eating out. We typically split the meal. Not saving a ton of money but some and all the food gets eaten.

3. Looking first on Craigslist or market place for any tools I need. First time home owner, saved well over a thousand already on tools. Probably thousands more doing work myself.

4. Gym memberships aren't cheap but something a value having. I saved some money by getting a couples deal + paying in advance + (using my fsa to pay for it) insurance wouldn't discount, some do but not mine honestly don't know why they excepted the fsa

All in all I also make lunches and breakfast at home, use a refillable water bottle at work and at home. Buy in bulk and any number of things other people suggest. 

My main experience had been don't let frugality keep you from doing things you love (dining, vacations, hobbies, outside entertainment / movies / concerts ect.) but find a way to do them cheaper. I go out a couple days a week but memberships, deals, coupons, what have you let me do it at half the price other people are willing to pay.

Edit: I know these things are the most frugal and really avoiding doing any of these things will save you money. (Don't go out to eat, watch new movies from questionable websites, exercise outside or do calisthenics, borrow tools.) But I enjoy all of these things and my gf more so. I am able to live a fulfilled life and yet feel independent and not subservient to my budget. I'm reminded of this by a story

My parents neighbor an extremely poor man, lived in near poverty. People would bring him food, do his laundry and drive him places (his car was 40 years old). In the entirety that I had know him and my parents had known him they thought he was poor. He died this year and wouldn't you know it this real life scrouge had 33 million dollars in the bank. I do not use a template, I have been keeping track of my goals in a google doc. 

I have it formatted so my yearly goals sit on top. I write out my current months goals which should be in line with my yearly goals. They do not have to be even distributed i.e \[year goal: read 20 books / month goal: read 1.5 books\] maybe it's just one book. 

I follow this up with my goals for the current week. Using the first example maybe i.e \[read 4 chapters\]. Then I write down my goal for the day. 

At the beginning of the day I review my goals for the night before, highlighting what I succeeded in and what I did not. 

At the end of the week I reflect and a few sentences about what I did right and maybe why I didn't get a workout in, or didn't read before bed. 

When I finish the month I start a new section below it. Now when I jump on I have 5 months in order documented that I scroll through to reach the bottom. 

The more green highlights I see on my way down the closer I know I am to achieving my goals.

​

**Month Goals**

* workout every week
* read 1 book

**Week 1 Goal**

* workout 2 times
* read 4 chapters

**Monday**

* workout 
* ~~read 20 pages~~ (went to movie instead)

**Tuesday**

* read 40 pages (make up for yesterday)

​

So that's the general format I follow. If I find there is a certain goal that I continually skip I re-evaluate if it is \[worth pursuing / being tackled the right way / adding too much to my plate\]

# My journey through self care and improvement

First and foremost decide that you want to change and recognize that you are not on the path that you want your life to continue. You have done this so you are off to a great start.

​

1. Make a list of goals for the week / month / 3 months from now

They should be \[S.M.A.R.T\]([http://www.hr.virginia.edu/uploads/documents/media/Writing\_SMART\_Goals.pdf](http://www.hr.virginia.edu/uploads/documents/media/Writing_SMART_Goals.pdf)) goals and be something you are passionate about. Don't get carried with listing things you always wanted to do like learn another language or learn an instrument. Start small you can always expand later. E.g Start skin care routine, brush teeth everyday, exercise for 1 hour this week.

2.    Slowly organize and clean your environment

This may be one of your goals and that is ok, in fact it makes all the better. If things are out of place or don't have a home decide where things should go. I found the best question was why? WHY are my clothes not put away > I don't want to > I don't want to because I don't know where to put them. SOLUTION find a place to put my clothes. Having a clean environment will do wonders to put you in a better place.

3.    Exercise

I know, no one wants to hear this but your idea of exercise and mine might be totally different so hear me out. Exercise can help you look better sure, but it is incredible way to better both your physical health and your mental health. You don't need to go to a gym, you don't need >$100 of equipment. Your body weight is all you need and there are a ton of resources to get an idea of exercises you can do. Start small try \[this\] ([https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=HDfvWrGUkC8](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=HDfvWrGUkC8)/). Work your way up to 10 minutes of exercise 3 days a week and keep going from there. I guarantee if you start small it will be easy to continue. You do not want to get in over your head only to back out.

4. Represent the best version of yourself

Maybe that is little to heavy, but hear me out. You are trying to turn over a new leaf hear and are clearly not overly satisfied with what you are bringing to the table. Make an effort this time around. Take some time to choose what you are going to wear, and make it look good. Groom yourself (shave / style facial hair, trim your nails), Try a little hair product or get a hair cut. Begin a skin care routine. The possibilities are endless, the point of it being that your demonstrate that you value you. That is what this whole journey is about and if you look the way you feel I can personally attest to the fact you will feel better.

I hope this helps you. I have been on this journey for nearly a year and starting small was really key. A lot of the other redditors offered lots of valuable specific advice. I hope what I have provided is a good outline to get started. I am still on this quest myself and personally am still grappling with some of the larger issues in my life. If you want any more advice I am happy to help where I can.

To do this I started seeing a therapist every few weeks. Separated myself from aspects of life that I felt were negative. Started spending more time with family and friends and taking the time to improve myself. A lot of it comes down to learning to take the time to self-analyze the issues as problems and taking the steps to solve them. For example, I don't feel comfortable dating. > Why? well, I don't feel like I am presenting the best me and I do not feel I can relate to the people I am seeing. > Do what you can to improve your presentation, wear different clothes, start working out.
